assessment.conclusion: Existing admission requires the same UID; report authorization additionally checks native socket peer PID and the live observer start/boot tuple. Stored observer, previously bound direct child, terminal outcome and independently gathered root must match. Reaped children are deliberately not probed at report time. Exact bounded decoders, parameterized SQL and static errors preserve the local threat boundary. A claimed root, environment token or group membership alone is insufficient. The read operation uses the same authenticated path and cannot launch work.

The sole waiter supplies a positive owned-child PID to wait4 and only consumes rusage on exited/signaled events. Timeval conversion is explicit user plus system seconds with no host normalization; invalid usage cannot replace the original exit status. The C workload uses separate getrusage SELF/CHILDREN calls and integer-microsecond arithmetic after explicit waits for both workers and all eight short-lived descendants. It shares native accounting semantics, not the Rust conversion/helper; it is an independent reference implementation, not an independent kernel. The small print/exit tail is acknowledged. Production correctly remains Partial for an opaque command even though this controlled fixture establishes matched waited scope.

assessment.topic: Ancestry, nested accounting and unrelated processes
assessment.conclusion: Private sidecar claims are tied to a stable live native ancestor and independently checked against daemon-captured ancestry/Traffic roots. Lifecycle-only and mixed-mode nesting use the same accounting-root mechanism. Included or unverified observations are non-additive; no implementation sums inclusive nested values. Missing/contradictory lineage remains unverified or is rejected. PID-1 boundary handling now matches between CLI and daemon. The SDK C fallback verifies only a positive-PID unreaped zombie and its parent; it does not wait, signal or collect a process group. The foreground acceptance includes a real OS pipe and independently measured CPU from an unrelated peer in the same group.

One Instant is captured immediately around the sole spawn attempt and frozen at terminal observation before completion/report I/O. Stop/continue does not reset it; includes_stopped is true. Queue wait uses separately persisted queued/reserved wall timestamps and a labeled basis, never a difference of daemon monotonic epochs or subtraction from run elapsed. Measurement-aware lifecycle-only registration establishes queue zero; legacy/missing/reversed intervals remain unknown. Undetectable wall-clock steps remain a limitation of the explicit wall-clock observation.

assessment.topic: Bounded fail-open, single execution and compatibility
assessment.conclusion: Accounting adds no execution path. Both legacy preparation fallbacks keep the original pre-spawn deadline instead of renewing it. The report deadline is captured as terminal observation plus 500ms before unchanged lifecycle completion; slow completion consumes that window. Same report/request identity is retained through bounded write/readback/retry; reconciliation cannot relaunch a child. Native exit/reraise still controls command outcome when metadata fails. Protocol-1 completion definitions and host snapshot core schema are byte-identical to accepted HEAD, with additive meter.report/summary operations. The retained accepted pre-Meter binary is exercised against current CLI and registered desktop reads.

Migration 0004 is additive; migrations 0001-0003 are unchanged. A job primary key and unique report ID, within the existing writer/transaction lane, preserve one immutable typed report. Identical retries return unchanged; conflicting report identity/payload does not overwrite. The first durable terminal/interruption anchor is preserved by COALESCE. Reads and bounded writer maintenance enforce the exact 90-day cutoff, protect active records/dependencies and leave minimal expiry proof without deleting lifecycle/Traffic ownership. Late reports and clock rollback cannot resurrect an expired payload. Legacy/interrupted/unavailable/missing/expired states remain distinct.

One summary rather than periodic samples uses the existing finite writer and cancellation/progress controls. Cleanup modifies at most 128 job keys per batch; it is not another writer/service. Native lineage walks have a 128-edge cap. Desktop summary uses the existing bounded read lane, adds no reporting proxy and retains serialized refresh behavior. No representative-load latency, throughput, memory or battery benchmark is claimed by this review.

assessment.topic: Inline selected-job interpretation and stable interaction
assessment.conclusion: The production registered read path feeds selected-job detail with CPU used in core-seconds, independent run elapsed and queue wait, visible Partial/Unknown reasons, scope, basis and exact identity disclosure. Numeric zero differs from unknown and tiny positive values. Selection/generation/connection guards reject late replies; immutable reports survive disconnect/restart while lookup freshness is labeled independently. Native details/summary controls, section-specific busy state and stable live text are covered by deterministic DOM assertions. This is not a contrast, screen-reader, enlarged-text or rendered-window result.

The additive schema has no argv, environment, cwd or arbitrary diagnostic fields. Exact decoders and local static error mapping reject extra/private payloads. Native acceptance checks an argv/environment/cwd sentinel against the reported summary, database/WAL and daemon logs. Existing command streams, exit/signals, completion decoders and host snapshot are preserved by the scoped diffs and backend regression receipt. The Traffic fault-test repair explicitly declines Meter and leaves original lost-ACK, permit and one-marker assertions intact.
